question: True or false: the parable of blind men each describing an elephant by one part appears in early Buddhist scripture?
answer: True. In the Udana, part of the Pali canon, the Buddha tells of a king who has blind men touch an elephant: the one at the head says a pot, the ear a winnowing basket, the tusk a ploughshare, until they come to blows. It is his picture of rival teachers clinging to partial views.
move: Each person holding a different part can be right and still wrong.
ask: In my latest disagreement, are we each holding a different part of the same elephant?
trap: Knowing it only from Jain, Sufi or nineteenth-century retellings.
reference: Ireland, The Udana: Inspired Utterances of the Buddha, Buddhist Publication Society, 1990
